d_cross.name: Solve an equation: graph both sides
steps: Open Desmos (top right of the test screen)
Line 1: type y = the LEFT side
Line 2: type y = the RIGHT side
Click the point where the two graphs cross
Read the x-value. Is that the FIND? If not, finish the last step

d_expr.name: Use Desmos as a calculator
steps: Type the whole expression on one line (use ( ) and / for fractions)
Read the answer on the right of the line

d_zeros.name: Find zeros (x-intercepts)
steps: Click the gray dots where the graph touches the x-axis
Read the x-values: those are the zeros / solutions

d_vertex.name: Find the vertex (min or max)
steps: Click the turning point (the gray dot at the bottom or top)
Read it: x = where it happens, y = the min/max VALUE

d_count.name: Count solutions
steps: Type both equations (or y = each side)
Count the crossing points: 0, 1, 2 … Same line = infinitely many

d_slider.name: Find a constant with a slider
steps: Type the equations with the letter (like k) in them
Drag k until the graph does what the question says (parallel, touches once, etc.)

d_table.name: Line from points or a table
steps: Type the x-values in x₁ and the y-values in y₁
On a new line type y₁ ~ m x₁ + b

d_check.name: Test the answer choices
steps: Line 1: type y = the original expression
Next lines: type y = each answer choice, one at a time
The choice that lies exactly on top of the original is right

d_ineq.name: Inequalities and points
steps: Type the inequality (use < > ≤ ≥ from the keyboard)
In the shaded part = a solution. On a dashed line = NOT a solution

d_stats.name: Mean and median
steps: Type mean([4, 8, 9, 11, 18]) with the real numbers
Type median([…]) on the next line if needed

t_calc.name: Calculator (TI Move 1–2)
steps: Type it left to right. Use ( ) around anything added before you divide
Fractions: use n/d. Percents: up 20% = × 1.20, down 20% = × 0.80
Press enter. Need a fraction? Press the toggle key

t_solver.name: Equation Solver (TI Move 3)
steps: Press ⌂, then 5 (Equation Solver). Old stuff? Press clear
E1 box: type the LEFT side (x is the X,T,θ,n key)
Arrow ▼. E2 box: type the RIGHT side
Press the top-row key under NEXT
Type 0 as a guess, press enter
Press the top-row key under SOLVE. Read X =

t_poly.name: Polynomial Root Finder (TI Move 4)
steps: ORDER = 2, then the top-row key under NEXT
Type a, then b, then c from ax² + bx + c = 0 (use the − on the right side for signs)
Press the top-row key under SOLVE. Read x1 and x2

t_system.name: System Solver (TI Move 5)
steps: Line up both equations as  x-number, y-number = number
Pick 2 equations, 2 unknowns, then the top-row key under NEXT
Type the 3 numbers for each equation
Press the top-row key under SOLVE. Read x and y

t_graph.name: Graph + trace (TI Move 6)
steps: Press y= and type the equation
Press 2nd, then trace (calc). Pick zero, minimum, maximum or intersect
Follow the prompts (left side, right side, guess) with the arrows and enter

t_store.name: Store & check (TI Move 7)
steps: Press sto→, then X,T,θ,n, then enter
Type the LEFT side, enter. Type the RIGHT side, enter
Both sides match = that choice is right

t_trig.name: Trig in degrees (TI Move 8)
steps: Press mode, arrow to DEGREE, press enter (2nd mode to quit)
Type sin( , cos( or tan( with the angle, then )

hand.name: No calculator
steps: This one is faster on paper than on any calculator
Write each step on your scratch paper (stuck? use Coach me up)
Use the calculator only to check the arithmetic

lin1: The solver does the algebra; then finish the FIND.
lin2: Mostly setting up the equation; test choices in Desmos if unsure.
linf: Plug in, or put points in a Desmos table.
sys: Two equations, two unknowns: the System Solver or the Desmos crossing.
ineq: Solve like an equation; Desmos shading to check points.
equiv: Graph the original and each choice; the exact overlap is right.
nleq: Quadratics: the Root Finder gives exact solutions; Desmos shows them as dots.
nlf: Desmos shows vertex, zeros and y-intercept with a click.
ratio: Set up the proportion, then one calculator line.

data1: Desmos mean() and median() are instant.

prob: Part ÷ the "given" total; toggle for a fraction.
